question.worked_solution:
The logarithms on the left-hand side share the same base, so we can combine them using the product rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{6}⁡(x+3)+{log}_{6}⁡(2-x) & =1 \\ {log}_{6}⁡[(x+3)(2-x)] & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the equation for $x$ using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+3)(2-x) & ={6}^{1} \\ 2x-{x}^{2}+6-3x & =6 \\ {x}^{2}+x & =0 \\ x(x+1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x=0$ or $x=-1.$

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting them back into the original equation: 

- Substituting $x=0$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{6}⁡(0+3)+{log}_{6}⁡(2-0) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{6}⁡(3)+{log}_{6}⁡(2) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{6}⁡(3\cdot 2) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{6}⁡(6) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ 1 & =1.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=0$ is a valid solution.

- Substituting $x=-1$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{6}⁡(-1+3)+{log}_{6}⁡(2-(-1)) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{6}⁡(2)+{log}_{6}⁡(3) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{6}⁡(2\cdot 3) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{6}⁡(6) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ 1 & =1.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=-1$ is a valid solution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$x=0$ and $x=-1$".
